rules.statement: Convert text to bytes and bytes to text only through `NCode.Buffers.SecureEncoding.UTF8`/`.ASCII` or an encoding constructed with `throwOnInvalidBytes: true`, never through lenient `Encoding.UTF8`/`Encoding.ASCII`.
rules.why: Lenient encodings silently replace unencodable characters with `?` or U+FFFD. Distinct inputs can then collide in signatures, hashes, derived keys and AAD.
rules.check: Look for `Encoding.UTF8`, `Encoding.ASCII`, `new UTF8Encoding()` without throwOnInvalidBytes, or similar lenient encodings used for GetBytes/GetString/GetByteCount.

rules.statement: Do not call overloads that pick an encoding implicitly. Call the overload that takes an explicit `SecureEncoding.UTF8` instead.
rules.why: An implicit default encoding is lenient and hides the same character-substitution defects.
rules.check: Look for stream writer/reader, File.ReadAllText/WriteAllText or similar text APIs called without an encoding argument.

rules.statement: Pass `contentEncoding: SecureEncoding.UTF8` explicitly on every `TypedResults.Text` and `TypedResults.Content` call. For a media type that has no charset parameter (such as `application/jwt`), write strict UTF-8 bytes yourself instead of passing an encoding.
rules.why: The analyzer cannot tell calls with an encoding from calls without one, so review must enforce it. Explicit strict UTF-8 keeps responses correct and correctly labeled.
rules.check: Look for `TypedResults.Text`/`TypedResults.Content` calls that have no contentEncoding argument or that pass a non-strict encoding, and for charset-less media types that get a charset added.

rules.statement: Let invalid or unrepresentable text throw from the strict encoding, and on inbound paths map that exception to the protocol's error response rather than substituting or stripping characters.
rules.why: Substituting characters turns malformed input into different, valid-looking input, for example a non-ASCII DPoP access token hashing like an ASCII one.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks that swallow encoding exceptions and continue with substituted text, and for inbound parsing that does not turn encoding failures into a protocol error. Values that must be ASCII (such as tokens) should be validated, e.g. with `Ascii.IsValid`.

rules.statement: Use strict encodings in test code too. When a test needs UTF-16 or a byte-order mark, build a strict encoding explicitly instead of using a lenient one.
rules.why: Tests that encode leniently pass on input the product rejects, which hides regressions.
rules.check: Look for lenient Encoding.* usage or `new UnicodeEncoding()` without throwOnInvalidBytes in test projects.
